L:working-out-load-centre:6: > A crate **1,200 mm** deep, pushed hard against the backrest → 1,200 ÷ 2 = **600 mm**.
L:working-out-load-centre:8: If the load **isn't hard against the backrest**, add the gap.
L:working-out-load-centre:10: > A **1,000 mm** deep load sitting **200 mm** away from the backrest → 200 + 500 = **700 mm**.
L:working-out-load-centre:11: That's why you **insert the tynes fully** — a gap pushes the load centre forward, past the 600 mm the rated capacity is based on. If the load centre is more than the data plate's load centre, **don't lift** — ask your supervisor.
L:working-out-load-centre:13: If one end is heavier (e.g. a machine with the motor at one end), the centre of gravity **isn't in the middle**. Check markings or paperwork for the centre of gravity, put the **heavy end towards the mast**, and ask your supervisor if you're unsure.
T:reading-a-load-chart: Checking a load against rated capacity, step by step
L:reading-a-load-chart:1: 1. **Weight** — work out how heavy the load is (Count → Multiply → Add the pallet).
L:reading-a-load-chart:2: 2. **Load centre** — check the load's centre is **no more than** the data plate's load centre (usually **600 mm**). If it's further out, **don't lift** — ask your supervisor.
L:reading-a-load-chart:3: 3. **Compare** — is the load **less than or equal to** the **rated capacity**? Yes → OK to lift. No → **do not lift**.
L:reading-a-load-chart:5: **Forklift A — rated capacity 2,500 kg at a 600 mm load centre.**
L:reading-a-load-chart:7:
A pallet weighs **1,900 kg** and its load centre is **600 mm**.
1,900 is less than 2,500 → **OK to lift.** You have 2,500 − 1,900 = **600 kg** to spare.
L:reading-a-load-chart:9:
A crate weighs **2.7 t**. 2.7 × 1,000 = **2,700 kg**.
2,700 is more than 2,500 → **Do not lift** — it's **200 kg over**.
L:reading-a-load-chart:11:
48 cartons of **50 kg** on a **30 kg** pallet: 48 × 50 = 2,400 → + 30 = **2,430 kg**.
2,430 is less than 2,500 → **OK to lift**, with **70 kg** to spare.
L:reading-a-load-chart:12: ## Worked example 4 — the most you can lift
L:reading-a-load-chart:13:
How many **600 kg** drums can Forklift A carry at once (on a drum carrier rated 2,500 kg)?
2,500 ÷ 600 = 4.17 → round **down** → **4 drums** (2,400 kg). Five would be 3,000 kg — too heavy.
L:reading-a-load-chart:14: > If the answer has a decimal, **always round down**. Rounding up puts you over the rated capacity.
L:travelling-safely:2: - Travel with the load **low** — just high enough to clear the ground and suit the surface (commonly around 100–150 mm) — and the mast **tilted back**.
L:travelling-safely:3: - Keep a **safe speed** for the load, surface and surroundings, within site limits.
L:travelling-safely:4: - **Look in the direction of travel.** If the load blocks your forward view, **travel in reverse** or use an **observer (spotter)**.
L:travelling-safely:5: - Use your **mirrors** and **sound the horn** at blind corners, doorways and intersections.
L:travelling-safely:6: - Turn **slowly** — especially when carrying a load.
L:travelling-safely:8: - Keep arms, legs and head **inside** the overhead guard.
L:travelling-safely:10: - **Loaded:** keep the **load on the uphill side** — drive **forwards up**, **reverse down**.
L:travelling-safely:11: - **Unloaded:** keep the **tynes pointing downhill** — reverse up, drive forwards down.
L:travelling-safely:12: - **Never turn** on a ramp or slope, and never travel across it.
L:travelling-safely:14: Follow the traffic management plan, use forklift routes, make eye contact, and **stop** if anyone enters your work area.
T:picking-up-and-stacking: Picking up, the trial lift and stacking
L:picking-up-and-stacking:1: 1. Approach **slowly and squarely**, tynes level, at the right height.
L:picking-up-and-stacking:2: 2. **Position the tynes** to suit the pallet or load — spread as wide as practical, load centred.
L:picking-up-and-stacking:3: 3. Insert the tynes **fully**, so the load is against the backrest.
L:picking-up-and-stacking:4: 4. **Trial lift:** lift the load just clear of its support and check — is the forklift stable? Is the load secure and balanced? If the rear wheels feel light or anything moves, **lower it straight away** and reassess.
L:picking-up-and-stacking:5: 5. **Tilt back** slightly, check behind you, and reverse out slowly.
L:picking-up-and-stacking:6: 6. **Lower to travel height** before moving off.
L:picking-up-and-stacking:8: - Check the **racking is compliant** and its capacity suits the load.
L:picking-up-and-stacking:9: - Approach squarely and **stop** before the rack.
L:picking-up-and-stacking:10: - Only raise or lower the load **when stationary**.
L:picking-up-and-stacking:11: - Raise to the required height, **level the tynes**, then **inch forward**.
L:picking-up-and-stacking:12: - Use **tilt and side shift** to position the load accurately.
L:picking-up-and-stacking:13: - Lower onto the beams, withdraw the tynes, then lower to travel height before moving.
L:picking-up-and-stacking:14: Use an **observer** whenever your view is restricted — agree hand signals first.
L:picking-up-and-stacking:15: ## Placing on an elevated flat surface (e.g. a mezzanine or truck deck)
L:picking-up-and-stacking:16: The surface must be **flat, stable and strong enough**. Use **gluts or dunnage** under unpalletised loads so you can withdraw the tynes cleanly.
L:loading-trucks:1: - Check the truck **can't move** — handbrake on, wheels chocked or vehicle restraint engaged, driver in a safe area away from the loading zone.
L:loading-trucks:2: - Set up an **exclusion zone** around the truck.
L:loading-trucks:3: - Check **dock plates** are secure and rated for the forklift plus load.
L:loading-trucks:4: - Check the trailer floor is sound and can take the weight.
L:loading-trucks:5: - Watch for **dock edges** — keep well back.
L:loading-trucks:8: - Make sure the ground is **firm and level**.
L:loading-trucks:9: - Watch for loads shifting on the deck when straps are removed — **check before unstrapping**.
L:shutting-down:1: Park in a **designated safe area** — never on a slope, and never blocking exits, walkways, fire equipment or electrical switchboards.
L:shutting-down:4: 3. **Lower the tynes** (or attachment) fully to the ground, tilted forward so the tips rest on the floor.
L:shutting-down:5: 4. Shut down as the manufacturer requires, **isolate the power source** (e.g. LPG valve or battery isolator, per site procedure) and **remove the key**.
L:shutting-down:7: 6. Do a **post-operational check** and record and report any defects from the shift.
L:lpg-and-batteries:1: - Only in a **well-ventilated area**, away from ignition sources — **no smoking** or naked flames.
L:lpg-and-batteries:2: - Wear **PPE** — gloves and eye protection. LPG can cause **cold burns**.
L:lpg-and-batteries:3: - **Close the cylinder valve** and let the engine run until it stops, then turn the ignition off.
L:lpg-and-batteries:4: - Disconnect and remove the cylinder; check the new cylinder's **valve, O-ring/seal and connection** for damage.
L:lpg-and-batteries:5: - Fit it with the **locating pin** in place and the cylinder secured.
L:lpg-and-batteries:6: - Open the valve slowly and **check for leaks** with soapy water or leak-detection solution — **never a flame**.
L:lpg-and-batteries:8: - Engine **off**, no smoking, in the designated refuelling area.
L:lpg-and-batteries:9: - Don't overfill; clean up spills straight away.
L:lpg-and-batteries:12: - Charging gives off **hydrogen gas**, which is explosive — the area must be **ventilated** and free of ignition sources.
L:lpg-and-batteries:13: - Wear **PPE** — battery acid is corrosive. Know where the **eyewash** station is.
L:lpg-and-batteries:14: - **Turn the charger off before connecting or disconnecting** the battery, to avoid sparks.
L:lpg-and-batteries:15: - Check cables and plugs for damage; follow the manufacturer's instructions for electrolyte levels.
Q:1:1:p: Which licence class covers a standard counterbalance forklift?
Q:1:1:e: LF is the forklift truck class. LO covers order-picking forklifts.
Q:1:2:p: What is the minimum age to hold a High Risk Work Licence?
Q:1:2:e: You must be at least 18 years old.
Q:1:3:p: You notice the forklift's horn isn't working. Under WHS law you must:
Q:1:3:e: Workers have a duty to report defects and hazards. Do not operate it until it's fixed.
Q:1:3:o1: Report it and not use the forklift until it is fixed
Q:1:3:o2: Use it carefully and mention it at the end of the shift
Q:1:3:o3: Fix it yourself without telling anyone
Q:1:3:o4: Ignore it if the area is quiet
Q:1:4:p: What is the main purpose of a code of practice?
Q:1:4:e: Codes of practice give practical guidance on how to meet duties under WHS laws.
Q:1:4:o2: It is the manufacturer's operating manual
Q:1:4:o3: It gives practical guidance on how to meet your WHS duties
Q:1:5:p: Where would you find how a particular forklift must be operated and serviced?
Q:1:5:e: The manufacturer's operator manual sets the requirements for that machine.
Q:1:6:p: Which of these is a workplace record a forklift operator should complete?
Q:1:6:e: Pre-start checklists, defect reports and incident reports are all records operators complete.
